final_takeaways: Nothing in this delta is authoritative. Every item is a candidate for librarian review.
9 candidate decisions, 7 open questions, 6 action items, 7 items deliberately not promoted.

The substantive change is CAND-DEC-001: the NDA becomes an electronic acknowledgement rather than a DocuSign e-signature, with one full signature at the end. The existing prototype models the NDA as a multi-state signing flow, so this is a build change (ACT-005).

CAND-Q-004 conflicts with DEC-001. Shawn Main is contemplating dropping the Wolfsberg questionnaire requirement outright, which would make DEC-001's fallback question set unnecessary rather than optional.
CAND-DEC-002 and CAND-DEC-003 are the first architectural calls in the ledger: everything inside Databricks on LakeBase, with authentication and the public UI outside it.

Three candidates are low confidence: CAND-DEC-007 (a UX takeaway restated, not decided here), CAND-DEC-008 (a design constraint with no mechanism) and CAND-DEC-009 (pre-empted by a call that had not yet happened).
CAND-DEC-002 bears on Q-002 in the registry — whether intake documents must be stored in Databricks — without answering it directly.
blocking_reasons: All candidates require librarian approval before any record or ticket can be created.
CAND-DEC-001 is gated on Jonathan confirming that an electronic acknowledgement is acceptable in place of DocuSign (CAND-Q-001).
CAND-DEC-006 has no specification behind it — the stages, criteria and limits are all open (CAND-Q-005) — and CAND-DEC-005 explicitly says to keep building minimally until they are settled.

Only 2 of the 11 parsed transcripts have been extracted, so an earlier position this meeting changes may exist in the record without a DEC- id to supersede. No prior decision establishing DocuSign as the NDA mechanism exists in the registry, so CAND-DEC-001 cannot cite a supersedes_id.
